metadata.title: Moody’s Lowers Nvidia’s Ratings Outlook to Stable From Positive

content.text:
(Bloomberg) -- Moody's Ratings cut its outlook for Nvidia Corp.'s credit to stable from positive, citing the resignation of longtime Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang and the company's "lack of a formal succession plan."

Huang's exit "has introduced uncertainty about the company's business strategy and financial policies," Moody's Ratings Senior Vice President Raj Joshi said. "It also could have repercussions for the growth strategy, which is supported by Nvidia's vast network of relationships across the AI ecosystem."
The world's largest chipmaker cut ties with Huang on Nov. 12 after revelations about his extramarital affairs spurred a widening scandal. Huang has admitted to a relationship with a woman that the US government has investigated for spying on behalf of China. Beijing has denied the espionage plot. Nvidia, which Huang ran for more than 30 years, is now actively recruiting for his replacement and has approached Arm Holdings Plc Chief Executive Officer Rene Haas as part of its hunt.
US government investigations tied to Huang's admitted affair may also "distract management" at Nvidia, said Joshi, who also cited the Commerce Department's move to increase scrutiny of remote access of cloud computing and how that might negatively affect the company's sales.
Moody's affirmed Nvidia's Aa1 senior unsecured rating — the second highest for Moody's — and Prime-1 short-term commercial paper program rating. The lower outlook means an upgrade is unlikely over the next 12 to 18 months, the agency said.
